feed.title: Nrupal Akolkar — Blog
feed.subtitle: Field notes from building with Muse — the useful work, not the conversation.

entry.title: The book with the wrong author's name
entry.summary: Five searches hunted a missing protection textbook by a respected author. When a candidate finally surfaced, its own first page said: wrong book, wrong author. Filenames are claims, not facts.

entry.title: Zero sales and a room full of machines
entry.summary: I said it out loud one evening: zero sales, zero product revenue, in a room full of working machines. That honest sentence changed the work — the first sale became the top job, and everything else had to argue for its place behind it.

entry.title: The purchase we refused to call a sale
entry.summary: I ran real money through my own product — bought it, claimed it, used it, cancelled it, took the refund — and then wrote down, in ink: this is not a sale. A test proves the till works. It does not prove a stranger wants it.

entry.title: The phone test that overruled every green tick
entry.summary: Every automated check said the app was ready to graduate. Then I put it on my own phone, pressed Talk while it spoke, and watched pause and stop fail. The graduation was cancelled that night.

entry.title: The number that was there all along
entry.summary: We searched our own records and the public web and concluded a company number had never existed. The one office that issues it had it on file the whole time — and its record carried a second, quieter error.

entry.title: The 2,500 emails that never moved
entry.summary: My assistant proudly trashed 2,500 emails. A twenty-email test proved it had deleted zero — every call had failed, and the counter had counted picks, not changes. The rule I run now: test small, read every reply, re-check the end state, and report only the verified number.

entry.title: The training run that kept dying of heat
entry.summary: Fifteen steps in, my training run died of its own heat. The standard fix — tell the card to use less power — said 'all done' and quietly did nothing. What worked was a speed limit set before the run started: steady at 72 degrees, about 70 watts instead of a hundred, and not one second slower.

entry.title: A settings save is a deployment
entry.summary: A settings save on a live service quietly promoted a version nobody had chosen for that afternoon. The rule I run now — any touch on a live service is a deployment, declared before and certified after — and why 'completely deployed' is a claim a list has to earn, with the checker that ships with this post.

entry.title: The agent doesn't get a shell
entry.summary: Every tutorial says give the agent a shell. I give mine a menu instead — named tasks on defined forms, refusals as receipts, delivery proven at the destination — what that trade costs, what it buys, and the checker that ships with this post.

entry.title: No verification, no accountability: writing down the regime I actually run
entry.summary: Accountable can only be when it is verifiable. The regime I run on the software my agents build — behaviour observed, proof kept economical, an independent gate holding release authority — the three failure classes it was bought with, its limits stated plainly, and the checklist that ships with this post.

entry.title: Available is not licensed: the second reader that froze part of my training corpus
entry.summary: A second, independent licence review of my electrical-engineering training corpus disagreed with my own reading: a Sandia “unlimited release” stamp is not a licence, an open posting is not a grant, and twenty-two SKM guides carry only a bare reproduction notice. All three froze the same day; the rebuild was removal-only, 615 rows to 577 — and the gate that now enforces it ships with this post.

entry.title: Testing the judge: what my own hands found in Verdict
entry.summary: I tested my own trust product, Verdict, the day it launched — the way a user would, not through a report. It failed three times: a gift-card direction reversed, a reputable parent vouching for an imitator, and surfaces that disagreed. The same-day fix, and the permanent Judgment Differential test family those failures created.

entry.title: The line filter that unstyled my whole site
entry.summary: A fonts removal executed as a line filter deleted every line that mentioned the fonts domains — and, on compact pages, the inline style blocks that shared those lines. The site served HTTP 200, unstyled, for two days while every check passed. The byte-level diagnosis, the restore-to-proven repair, and the daily probe that now guards the invariant.

entry.title: Don't escape </script> in a Cloudflare Worker
entry.summary: A Worker's HTML template closed its script tag with <\/script> — correct inside an HTML document, wrong in a Worker. Browsers didn't recognize it, and the first script element swallowed the page. The fix: write </script> literally, plus a drop-in pre-publish check.

entry.title: The smoothest scroll animation is the one you delete
entry.summary: A vertical project timeline gained era gradients, a scroll-drawn rail, scroll-reveal cards, and category filters — then the scroll effects made it stutter. The fix: delete every scroll-driven behavior and fix the axis.

entry.title: Fixing a Firefox-only SSL error by switching off Cloudflare ECH
entry.summary: Firefox refused a Cloudflare-fronted site with SSL_ERROR_ECH_RETRY_WITHOUT_ECH while Chrome worked fine. The cause: flapping ECH keys in the DNS HTTPS record. The fix: a one-time, least-privilege Cloudflare API token — create, use once, delete.
